text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered -> SEV2: qatalyst (enterprise-vpc) prefix hit-rate collapse detected for tenant q-102. 95th latency spike and 5xxs rising. @oncall-page sent. Paging: @Maya Patel

Maya Patel: On it. Pulling up KV stats for q-102. Any immediate mitigation suggestions? :eyes:

Samir Khan: Likely prefix pollution / prefetch loop. I've seen similar with their long-tail prefixes. Can someone grab kv diagnostics: `kv.sh stats --tenant q-102 --prefixes 10m` and tail the runtime logs for prefetch worker.

Jason Li: Running now. Output snippet (tail):
```
2026-08-12T02:12:11Z prefetcher[worker-3] INFO prefetch requested prefix="usr:profile:"
2026-08-12T02:12:11Z runtime cache_hit_rate tenant=q-102 prefix_total=9 prefix_hitrate=0.02
2026-08-12T02:12:12Z routing serve request id=.. tenant=q-102 model=gpt-small latency_ms=3400
2026-08-12T02:12:15Z prefetcher[worker-3] WARN prefetch-amplification detected count=120
```

Jason Li: Hitrate at ~2% for hot prefixes, prefetcher is flooding KV with unique prefixes (prefetch amplification).

Maya Patel: Customer impact? @qatalyst-sre any report?

qatalyst-sre: Yes, witnessed elevated p95 and a small burst of 5xxs on their edge. Business critical endpoints are slow (~3-4s p95). They called support and are watching. They have traffic ~120r/s from a small set of product flows.

Samir Khan: Proposed immediate mitigations (in order):
1) Suspend prefetch for tenant q-102.
2) Evict large prefix buckets and reduce per-tenant prefetch concurrency.
3) If still bad, pin tenant to isolated cache (dedicated pool) or enable cache-disable-fallback to bypass polluting cache.

Maya Patel: I'll suspend prefetch first. Command: `infractl prefetch suspend --tenant q-102 --reason "suspected amplification"`

Jason Li: Done -> `infractl` returned 200. Prefetch workers for q-102 stopped. Confirmed no new prefetch jobs in the tail.

DevInfra-bot: Action logged: prefetch suspend by Maya Patel at 2026-08-12T02:17:03Z (ticket INC-2026-2117).

Samir Khan: Good. Now let's evict stale prefix cache entries for q-102 to free space: `kvctl evict --tenant q-102 --scope prefixes --age-gt 1h --confirm`

Jason Li: Running eviction...

Jason Li: Eviction completed: 48k prefix keys removed, estimated freed 23GB. Monitoring hit-rate.

Maya Patel: Observability: p95 fell from ~3400ms -> ~1800ms within 90s, error rate down from 1.2% -> 0.6%. Progressing but not fully recovered.

Samir Khan: That makes sense — cache warmed poorly now. Next step: enable per-tenant isolation mode (soft isolation) to prevent cross-tenant pollution: `kvctl isolation enable --tenant q-102 --mode soft` This will allocate an isolated prefix namespace and limit eviction bleed.

Jason Li: Enabled isolation. Logs show isolation allocation to node pool `dedicated-shortburst-3`.

DevInfra-bot: Action logged: quarantine/isolation enabled by Jason Li at 2026-08-12T02:24:11Z.

qatalyst-sre: Thanks team. We're seeing better consistency now; some endpoints still 1.5-2s. They're asking if there's any chance of a config change on our side that triggered this.

Maya Patel: We should check for recent client-side changes (increased unique prefixes). But immediate is to throttle noisy flows at the gateway for q-102 while cache warms: `edgectl rate-limit --tenant q-102 --route /api/profiles --limit 80r/s`

Jason Li: Applied gateway throttle. Traffic dropped to ~85r/s for that route. Observing latency.

Maya Patel: Latency p95 -> ~950ms after throttle + isolation + eviction. Error rate ~0.2%. Looks stable.

Samir Khan: Follow-up mitigations to avoid recurrence:
- Enforce per-tenant prefetch caps (max prefix growth per minute)
- Prevent prefetching of highly-unique user keys by thresholding by cardinality
- Add telemetry for prefetch amplification detection with automatic suspend
- Consider permanent dedicated cache pool for qatalyst if their access pattern remains high-cardinality

Priya Rao: Heads-up: I'm taking the on-call handoff from Maya. Summary for handoff: prefetch suspended, eviction completed, isolation enabled, gateway throttle applied, p95 recovered to <1s. Customer engaged. I'll keep watching and coordinate postmortem.

Maya Patel: Handoff ack. Please escalate to platform if we see re-emergence or if isolation causes capacity pressure.

Priya Rao: Will do. Adding follow-ups to INC-2026-2117:
- action: telemetry rule for prefetch amplification (owner: eng-runtime)
- action: per-tenant prefetch limits (owner: eng-ml)
- action: customer-facing summary + RCA timeline (owner: support)

qatalyst-sre: We appreciate the quick response. We'll search client side for any recent rollout that may have increased unique prefixes. We'll share findings in the next hour.

Samir Khan: One more note — if eviction + isolation weren't effective we were ready to pin tenant to a dedicated LRU pool (`pinning -> qatalyst-ded-1`) and enable cold-cache fallback for non-critical endpoints. That path is still available.

DevInfra-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV3 by Maya Patel at 2026-08-12T02:40:11Z after stability confirmed.

Priya Rao: Closing loop for now. I'll monitor for 2 hours and update INC-2026-2117 with timeline. If any increase in hot-prefix unique growth is observed, we'll schedule an emergency config change window with the customer. :white_check_mark:

Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. Postmortem to be scheduled for next week once we have telemetry and customer confirmation.

incident-bot: Note: This thread will be archived in 7 days.
